P/anticipatory-application: our own observation, not Sheehan's -- this chapter engages pathos exclusively via De Interpretatione's psychological pathemata and Metaphysics IX's ontological dynamis tou pathein, never via Rhetoric II's taxonomy of persuasive emotions (anger, fear, pity, etc.) -- an adjacent but textually distinct lineage of the same Greek root, worth tracking against the dissertation's Part I material

P/anticipatory-application: Sheehan's ontological pathos (receptivity/dynamis tou pathein, a being's capacity to be acted upon) is a plausible deep metaphysical substrate for Rhetoric II's pathe (the audience's being-moved/persuaded) as a species of pathein generally -- a genealogical link Sheehan himself does not draw, offered here as our own cross-reference

P/anticipatory-application: Sheehan's culminating equation pathos = facticity = the factum sharpens Part II's own vocabulary for distinguishing existentiel/psychological affect from existential-structural attunement, directly relevant to the phantasma/originary terminology lock
